newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thailand seeks diesel, gasoline on output problems.
newsitem.headline: Thailand seeks diesel, gasoline on output problems.

text.p: Shutdowns of crude units at three Thai refineries in January and early February has stalled all gasoline and diesel exports from Thailand with some refiners now looking to import diesel and gasoline to tide over the unexpected shortage, industry sources said on Thursday.

Sources said the tightening of supplies in Thailand started when Bangchak Petroleum Plc closed a 40,000 barrels-per-day crude distillation unit (CDU) for a 2-week scheduled maintenance in the second half of January.
At around the same time Star Petroleum Refinery Co shutdown part of its 130,000-bpd refining capacity for about one-week, the source said.
Prior to this, Thai Petrochemical Industry had closed its 65,000-bpd condensate splitter for around 10-days in early January due to operational problems.
All refineries are currently operating at normal capacity, sources said.
As a result of these earlier shutdowns at least two 30,000-tonne diesel cargoes were exported to Thailand for February delivery from Singapore, sources said.
The sources said the refineries were seeking further diesel barrels to help build up stocks amid strong domestic demand.
The source said Thailand is not likely to export any spot gasoline cargoes in February and March due to the supply squeeze and strong post-monsoon domestic demand.
One refiner is now heard seeking a 95-octane cargo for first half March arrival.
